method: ENTIRELY from AMH: the Drug choice for selected infections page and ALL NINE of its tables, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED. No passage reproduced, no source_text stored, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable, and every drug choice must be verified by a person against a current subscription. ⚠️ AMH'S OWN FIRST SENTENCE IS CARRIED AS THE GUIDELINE'S FIRST LINE: these tables are not intended to supplant local protocols or management advice from clinical microbiologists or infectious diseases specialists. ⚠️ THE TABLES NAME DRUGS AND DURATIONS BUT NOT DOSES: not one milligram figure appears in any of the nine, so this guideline gives drug, route and duration and NO DOSE. That is AMH's structure, not an omission in retrieval, and it is stated on the face of the guideline. The two open sources AMH points to -- the Australian STI Management Guidelines and the 2025 Australasian C. difficile guidelines -- were NOT retrieved.

claims.claim: BACTERIAL MENINGITIS, empirical treatment ON ADMISSION TO HOSPITAL: first choice IV CEFOTAXIME OR IV CEFTRIAXONE, alternative IV MOXIFLOXACIN, again starting dexamethasone with or before the first antibacterial dose if possible

claims.claim: In bacterial meningitis ADD VANCOMYCIN IF THERE ARE GRAM-POSITIVE COCCI IN THE CSF or if there is known penicillin-resistant pneumococcus, and ADD IV BENZYLPENICILLIN -- or IV trimethoprim with sulfamethoxazole -- IF AT HIGH RISK OF LISTERIA INFECTION, for example over 50 years, immunocompromised, or if Listeria is suspected

claims.claim: ENDOCARDITIS PROPHYLAXIS for HIGH-RISK patients having certain DENTAL procedures or upper respiratory tract interventions, viridans streptococcus group: first choice ORAL, IV OR IM AMOXICILLIN or IV/IM AMPICILLIN, alternative ORAL OR IV CLINDAMYCIN. GIVE A SINGLE DOSE BEFORE THE PROCEDURE; if oral is not possible give IV or IM; USE CLINDAMYCIN IN PENICILLIN HYPERSENSITIVITY OR IF A BETA-LACTAM HAS BEEN USED MORE THAN ONCE WITHIN THE PREVIOUS MONTH
